Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] [[Governor of Wisconsin|Governor]] [[Jim Doyle]] ran for re-election to a second term in office. He was unopposed in the Democratic primary, and faced [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] [[Mark Andrew Green|Mark Green]], who was unopposed in the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] primary, in the general election. The campaign between Doyle and Green was competitive and hotly contested, but Doyle, whose approval ratings hovered around 50%, had the upper hand.{{Cite web | url=http://www.surveyusa.com/50State2006/50StateGovernor060921State.htm |title = SurveyUSA {{pipe}} America's Neighborhood Pollster}} In the end, Doyle defeated Green by a fairly comfortable margin,
